name: All Threes (Dominoes)
description: All Threes is a classic 'point-scoring' domino game from the Muggins family. While the more common 'All Fives' focuses on multiples of five, All Threes requires players to calculate multiples of three to score. It is a game of quick mental arithmetic and positional blocking.

overview.description: All Threes is a classic 'point-scoring' domino game from the Muggins family. While the more common 'All Fives' focuses on multiples of five, All Threes requires players to calculate multiples of three to score. It is a game of quick mental arithmetic and positional blocking.

history.origins: Part of the European layout games that emerged in the 18th and 19th centuries. It is the direct sibling to All Fives and the combined game 'Fives and Threes', which is a staple of British pub culture.
timeline: 1800s: Muggins games (scoring layouts) gain popularity in Europe.
1900s: All Threes becomes a recognized standalone variant in domino strategy books.
Present: Popular in digital domino suites and European social clubs.
history.cultural: Commonly played alongside 'All Fives' as a training game for the more complex combined version popular in British leagues.
history.evolution: The game simplified the complex 'spinner' rules of American All Fives to focus on a standard two-ended line layout, emphasizing the 'Threes' math.

setup.players: 2 (7 tiles each), 3 (5 tiles each), or 4 (5 tiles each).
setup.dealing: Tiles are 'shuffled' face down (the 'wash'). Players draw their hand; remainders go to the 'Boneyard'.
setup.equipment: Domino tiles, cribbage board or score sheet.

rules.objective: Be the first to reach a target score (usually 150 or 250) by making the ends of the layout sum to a multiple of three.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Opening**: The player with the highest double leads (or by agreement). 2. **Matching**: Subsequent players must match the pips of one of the two open ends of the line. 3. **Scoring**: After each play, add the pips on the two exposed ends. If the total is divisible by 3, you score 1 point for every 3 in that total. For example: Sum 9 = 3 pts, Sum 12 = 4 pts, Sum 15 = 5 pts, Sum 18 = 6 pts. 4. **Drawing**: If a player cannot move, they must draw from the Boneyard until they can play or the boneyard is empty.
keyRules: Doubles: Placed crosswise. For scoring, you count the TOTAL pips on the double (e.g., a Double-6 counts as 12).
No Spinner: Only the two ends of the single line are ever open for play.
Blocked Game: If no one can play and the boneyard is empty, the player with the lowest pip count in their hand wins the hand's residue points.

strategy.basic: Prioritize making a scoring move over simply getting rid of high tiles. A 4-point move (sum 12) is worth more than 'dumping' a Double-6 for no points.
strategy.intermediate: Blocking: If you cannot score, play a tile that makes the end total a number that is difficult for the opponent to divide by 3 (like 7, 8, or 11).
strategy.advanced: Boneyard Management: If you have a strong hand, try to 'clog' the ends with values you don't have, forcing the opponent to draw from the boneyard and increase their hand size (and your eventual domino bonus).
tips: The highest possible score in one turn is 6 points (Sum 18). This happens if one end is a Double-6 (12) and the other is a 6.

variations.name: Fives and Threes
variations.description: The combined British favorite. Points are scored for multiples of 3 AND multiples of 5.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes only scoring multiples and league traditions; engine structure is otherwise shared.

variations.name: Block All Threes
variations.description: No boneyard drawing. If you can't play, you simply pass.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant keeps the same layout and scoring with a house rule that players never draw from the boneyard.

scoring.description: Scoring is done incrementally during play and a bonus is given at the end of each hand.
scoring.winCondition: First player to reach the target score wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: A sophisticated variant of Muggins where players must make the ends add up to multiples of three. Sharpen your math and your strategy to reach 250 points first.

hero.title: ALL THREES
hero.subtitle: The Arithmetic Choice
hero.tagline: Master the multiples. Dominate the line.
